hints: Look at what the colours mean and when they change. Brown means no starch yet, black means starch is present, so the time taken to first turn black tells you the rate for each starting concentration from 0 to 35.

Compare the columns from left to right. As glucose phosphate increases up to 25, the black colour appears earlier and earlier, but 30 and 35 both turn black at 1 minute. Think about what it means when adding more substrate stops speeding things up.
walkthrough:
**Work out what the iodine test is telling you**

Great start, let's decode the grid together. Iodine stays brown when there is no starch, and turns black-blue when starch is present.

So the time to the first black dot in each column is the time taken to make detectable starch. Shorter time means faster rate.

**Read the trend across substrate concentrations**

Now scan left to right. At $5 \ mg \ dm^{-3}$ black first appears at 8 minutes, at $15 \ mg \ dm^{-3}$ at 6 minutes, at $20 \ mg \ dm^{-3}$ at 5 minutes, at $25 \ mg \ dm^{-3}$ at 3 minutes.

Then at $30 \ mg \ dm^{-3}$ and $35 \ mg \ dm^{-3}$ black first appears at 1 minute in both. So rate increases with substrate up to about 30, then levels off.

**Apply limiting factors to explain it**

This is classic enzyme kinetics. When more substrate gives a faster rate, substrate concentration is limiting the rate because active sites are often empty and waiting.

That happens at $25 \ mg \ dm^{-3}$ or less. Above that, all active sites are saturated, so adding more substrate makes no further difference and another factor, like enzyme concentration, becomes limiting.

options.A: It is true that starch is being made from glucose phosphate, which is why iodine turns black, but this statement alone does not explain why the time to turn black changes with substrate concentration.
options.B: Rate is still increasing after 20, since 25 turns black at 3 minutes and 30 turns black at 1 minute, so maximum rate is not reached at 20.
options.C: Correct. At 25 and below, increasing glucose phosphate shortens the time to black, so rate increases with substrate. This shows substrate is the limiting factor in this range.
options.D: Enzyme concentration is the same in all tubes. If enzyme were limiting at low substrate, adding more substrate would not increase the rate, but it clearly does.
